newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PT sees European strategic partner - paper.
newsitem.headline: PT sees European strategic partner - paper.

text.p: Portugal Telecom expects to form a strategic alliance with a European partner or partners in March, its president Murteira Nabo was quoted as saying.
He told the weekend weekly Expresso newspaper in an interview: "The alliance will be in March."

Asked whether it would involve European or North American partners, he said: "I would say that our alliance is essentially European because 70 percent of our (telecommunications) traffic is in Europe. The fundamental component of our alliance has to be European."
Nabo said a strategic partnership was essential for PT to survive in the international market place.
"The alliance is a fundamental strategic component without which I (PT) cannot survive because I cannot be alone in this market," he said.
"The experience of European countries is clear: practically everybody has already joined an alliance or is preparing to join."
Nabo said PT was charging its consumers high prices and was preparing to bring prices down.
"Every one knows that our prices are high," he said. "National long distance and international calls are expensive. Local calls are not (by European standards)."
Asked if he was preparing to lower prices, he said: "I am. Of course I am." He gave no further details.
Nabo said he was preparing for the possible arrival of energy company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal in the local market as Portugal's second fixed telecommunications operator.

Asked if the second operator was condemned to fail in the local telecommunications market, Nabo said: "It is not necessarily condemned to failure. I think that we will share the market between us. I admit that the struggle for market share will be hard fought."
